title: Deferred KV provenance shuttle for intermittent SDKs
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: Edge and browser-adjacent SDKs (mobile, edge workers, IoT) are sensitive to extra per-request allocations and blocking path work from full provenance stamping and KV context attach. Some SDKs drop headers during intermittent connectivity or stream responses where immediate header enrichment is expensive.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, bounded "shuttle" that defers the final KV/provenance attach until a short, configurable window after the request lifecycle completes or when a safe flush point occurs. The shuttle should: reduce cold-path overhead for request handlers; support streaming/long-poll responses; provide backpressure signals to clients when buffer pressure is high; and remain compatible with existing sampling and trace-reconciliation logic.

Why different: Existing work focuses on in-flight span stitching and immediate propagation. This ticket introduces a deferred, memory-bounded proxy shuttle that shifts attach work off the hot path and provides explicit pressure signals to SDKs so they can adapt (throttle metadata attach, batch draws).
acceptance_criteria: Introduces a shuttle service/library that can be toggled in SDKs and the edge runtime
Per-request CPU overhead introduced by shuttle hot path < 1ms median on p50 for 95th percentile request types
Memory usage per active request capped (configurable default 64KB) and enforced with eviction policy
Trace/span linkage preserved end-to-end (reconciled IDs within 2s of final attach) and validated by trace-join tests
Shuttle exposes HTTP headers for backpressure (X-Redwood-Shuttle-Pressure: low|medium|high) and documented client behavior
Graceful fallback: if shuttle fails or is disabled, system falls back to immediate attach with metric flagging
E2E tests cover streaming responses, websocket reconnects, and intermittent connectivity scenarios
technical_notes: Core idea: allocate a tiny 'shuttle envelope' on the hot path that contains a stable request id + pointer to a bounded KV delta buffer. Defer serializing/attaching full provenance until later flush or when a client acknowledges a flush point.
Buffer eviction policy: LRU with walk-away eviction when total shuttle memory > configured pool (default 256MB node-wide), emit metric redwood.shuttle.eviction.count
Backpressure: runtime sets X-Redwood-Shuttle-Pressure header; SDKs will disable non-essential metadata attach if header=high

Trace reconciliation: reconciliation worker consumes shuttle queue, attaches final provenance, writes a reconciliation event to tracing backend. Sampling decisions are forwarded to worker to avoid double-counting.
API compatibility: implementable as middleware for HTTP/GRPC and a small shim for web sockets. Provide Node/Python/Go SDK helpers.
Security: provenance payloads remain encrypted-in-transit; no new sensitive fields introduced. Shuttle should honor KMS/HSM policies already in place for customer-managed keys.
rollout_plan: Implement shuttle library with feature flag default=off in SDKs
Deploy runtime shuttle queue with metrics and eviction policy to staging cluster
Enable feature flag for internal teams and run 2 week canary on internal services (console + internal ingestion) to measure overhead and reconciliation delays
Gradual rollout to customers by opt-in token, monitor shuttle.eviction.count and shuttle.reconcile.latency
If regressions detected, toggle feature off and auto-fallback to immediate attach; postmortem and adjustments
qa_tests: Microbenchmarks: measure hot-path overhead with and without shuttle across representative SDKs
Stress test: simulate high concurrency with small-memory shuttle pool to validate eviction and backpressure signals
Integration: websocket stream reconnects where final attach occurs after reconnect; verify single reconciled span
Chaos: kill reconciliation worker mid-reconcile and ensure graceful degradation and metric alerts
Tracing correctness: compare trace graphs before/after shuttle reconciliation using synthetic traces
